rows.what the ink shows: A continuous upper hook and lower leftward sweep support 5, followed by a separate rounded dot. The proposed closing parenthesis lies along the torn paper edge; the small surviving dark remnant does not establish its full curved stroke.

After the written u_1, a tall right-curving hooked stroke survives through a thick horizontal cancellation, making a closing parenthesis plausible. Separate comma and ellipsis points, and their total extent, cannot be recovered beneath the crossing stroke.

The raised character has a left descending entry followed by a distinct right arch and descending terminal. Those two stem portions support n, rather than the single upper curve and diagonal of 2; the cancellation crosses the lower portion.

A baseline u with two upright sides is visible at the right. At the left, cancellation crosses a triangular or looped body and a small raised curved mark; the raised mark may be n above Lambda or cancellation residue, while a distinct lower n cannot be securely separated.
One compact a-shaped loop with a short rising right terminal follows Car. The intervening paper is blank enough to exclude separate on letters before it.

The surviving upper stroke descends leftward, turns right and ends in a short low stem, closely matching the earlier cursive 4 on this page. It lacks the paired opposing lobes visible in the same-page 3; cancellation merges with the lower tip.

The small index immediately below the closing norm bars has a bent upper stroke, diagonal return and a short rightward foot. It is visibly curved and footed rather than the single upright stroke of 1.

A clear dot stands above the short descending i stroke, and a separate lower horizontal stroke supplies the final n. A thick horizontal run joins the left side of the dotted i body; its connection does not distinguish an extra preceding n from a long entry stroke of i.
